source.text: תְּהִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥דאֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣ אֱלוֹהַ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲבָרֲכָ֥ה שִׁ֝מְךָ֗ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: A praise of David. I will exalt you, my God, the King, and I will bless your name forever and ever.

en.L: A praise of David. I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God, the King, and I will bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever and ever.
en.B: A song of praise. Of David. My God, the King, I will lift {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} high in praise and bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name for ever and ever.
en.R: A song of praise. By David. My God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the King! I will tell how great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. I will always praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, forever and ever.

decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a praise: a song of praise (tehillah)
decisions.reason: This is the only psalm whose title calls it "a praise" (tehillah). The plural of the same word, tehillim, "praises", is the Hebrew name of the whole book of Psalms.

The psalm is an acrostic: its verses begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, from aleph (verse 1) to taw (verse 21). The line for the letter nun, which should come after verse 13, is missing from the Hebrew text (see the note on verse 13).
When people bless God (barakh), they do not give him anything; they praise him and speak of his goodness (103:1).
Balanced and Readable say what kind of praise is meant: the psalm is a song.

decisions.choice: My God, you are the King! I will tell how great you are
alternatives: I will exalt you, my God, the King
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title "the King" into a short statement and says what it is to exalt God: to say how great he is.

source.text: בְּכָל־י֥וֹם אֲבָרֲכֶ֑ךָּ וַאֲהַלְלָ֥ה שִׁ֝מְךָ֗ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: In every day I will bless you, and I will praise your name forever and ever.

en.L: Every day I will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and I will praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever and ever.
en.B: Day after day I will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and give praise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name for ever and ever.
en.R: I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} every single day. I will keep on praising {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever and ever.

decisions.choice: your name: you as you have made yourself known
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he has shown who he is (5:12; 9:11).
Readable uses "praise" for both verbs, since blessing God means praising him (145:1).

source.text: גָּ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝לִגְדֻלָּת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Great [is] YHWH and praised exceedingly, and to his greatness there [is] no searching.

en.L: Great [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to be praised exceedingly, and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness [there is] no searching.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great, worthy of the highest praise, and there is no searching out the depth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great! He deserves all our praise. No one can ever find the end of how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: praised exceedingly: deserving to be praised highly
decisions.reason: The form (mehullal) is "praised"; it can say that he is praised or that he is to be praised. The same line stands in 48:2 and 96:4.

decisions.choice: there is no searching: it can never be fully explored
decisions.reason: Nothing is beyond his greatness: no search can reach its limit (Job 11:7; Isaiah 40:28).

decisions.choice: No one can ever find the end of how great he is
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m2).

source.text: דּ֣וֹר לְ֭דוֹר יְשַׁבַּ֣ח מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וּגְב֖וּרֹתֶ֣יךָ יַגִּֽידוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Generation to generation will laud your works, and your mighty deeds they will declare.

en.L: Generation to generation will laud {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty deeds they will declare.
en.B: Each generation will praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works to the one after it and announce {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty acts.
en.R: Parents will tell their children about the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done. They will tell about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} powerful acts.

decisions.reason: The verb (shibbach) means to praise or extol; with "to generation" it pictures each generation praising God's works to the one that follows (78:4).
The word (gevurot) is acts that show strength, such as God's acts of rescue for Israel (106:2).
Readable makes the passing on from one generation to the next concrete: older people telling younger ones.

source.text: הֲ֭דַר כְּב֣וֹד הוֹדֶ֑ךָ וְדִבְרֵ֖י נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֣יךָ אָשִֽׂיחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] splendor of [the] glory of your majesty and [the] matters of your wonders I will meditate on.

en.L: The splendor of the glory of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty, and the matters of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders, I will meditate on.
en.B: I will reflect on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty, its glory and splendor, and on the story of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders.
en.R: I will think about how glorious and majestic {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. I will think about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

decisions.choice: the splendor of the glory of your majesty: your glorious and majestic splendor
decisions.reason: Three words for greatness are piled up (hadar, kavod, hod) to say that God's majesty is beyond words.

decisions.choice: the matters of your wonders: your wonderful works and the words that tell them
decisions.reason: The word (devarim) can mean words or matters. Here it may be the accounts of God's wonders, or simply the wonders themselves.
The verb (siach) means to think something through and also to talk about it (77:13; 105:2).

decisions.choice: I will meditate: the Hebrew text
alternatives: they will speak (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "I will meditate". The ancient Greek translation has "they will speak" in the first half and "they will tell" in the second, as in verses 6 and 11. The renderings follow the Hebrew text.

source.text: וֶעֱז֣וּז נוֹרְאֹתֶ֣יךָ יֹאמֵ֑רוּ וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ֥ אֲסַפְּרֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] might of your awesome [deeds] they will tell, and your greatness I will recount it.

en.L: And the might of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} awesome [deeds] they will tell, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness, I will recount it.
en.B: People will speak of the power of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fearsome deeds, and I will tell of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness.
en.R: People will talk about the powerful and frightening things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done, and I will tell how great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: your greatness: the words follow the form to be read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in one form and its notes say to read it in another; the written form is plural, "your great deeds", and the form to be read is singular, "your greatness". The renderings follow the form to be read; the meaning is nearly the same.

decisions.choice: your awesome deeds: deeds that make people afraid
decisions.reason: The word (nora'ot) is from the verb "fear": things so great that they cause awe and dread, like the acts at the Exodus (Deuteronomy 10:21).
"They" is anyone who sees God's works, as in verse 4. The psalmist joins them ("I will recount").
Balanced and Readable name who "they" are (m3).

source.text: זֵ֣כֶר רַב־טוּבְךָ֣ יַבִּ֑יעוּ וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] remembrance of [the] abundance of your goodness they will pour forth, and [of] your righteousness they will shout for joy.

en.L: The memory of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} abundant goodness they will pour forth, and [of] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness they will shout for joy.
en.B: They will spill over with the memory of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great goodness and sing out for joy at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.
en.R: People will remember how very good {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are, and they will not be able to stop talking about it. They will sing happily about how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always do what is right.

decisions.choice: remembrance: the memory and the telling of it
decisions.reason: The word (zekher) is a memory kept alive by being spoken about.

decisions.choice: pour forth: bubble over, speak freely
decisions.reason: The verb (nava') is used of a spring gushing water (Proverbs 18:4) and of words that pour out (19:3).

decisions.choice: righteousness: God doing what is right
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his faithfulness to do what is right, which often means rescuing his people (71:15).

decisions.choice: they will not be able to stop talking about it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a spring that overflows (m2).

decisions.choice: how you always do what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says what righteousness means here (m3).

source.text: חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֣וּם יְהוָ֑ה אֶ֥רֶךְ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם וּגְדָל־חָֽסֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: Gracious and compassionate [is] YHWH, long of anger and great of loyal love.

en.L: Gracious and compassionate [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, slow to anger and great in loyal love.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is full of grace and compassion, slow to anger and great in loyal love.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is kind and tender. He does not get angry quickly, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is great.

decisions.reason: The LORD's description of himself to Moses (Exodus 34:6), repeated through the Bible (86:15; 103:8; Joel 2; Jonah 4:2).

decisions.choice: long of anger: slow to become angry
decisions.reason: Anger was pictured by the nose (the same word, 'af), and a "long" nose is anger that is slow to rise.
The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith, the commitment God has bound himself to toward his people (Exodus 34:6-7). Literal and Balanced say "loyal love".
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
Readable uses plain words for the two qualities: grace that gives freely and the tender love of a parent (raham is related to the word for the womb).

source.text: טוֹב־יְהוָ֥ה לַכֹּ֑ל וְ֝רַחֲמָ֗יו עַל־כָּל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Good [is] YHWH to all, and his compassions [are] over all his works.

en.L: Good [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to all, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} compassions [are] over all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good to everyone; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} compassion covers all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good to everyone. He shows tender love to everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.

decisions.choice: his compassions: his tender love, shown again and again
decisions.reason: The plural (rachamim) is the usual form for compassion; it is the same root as "compassionate" in verse 8.

decisions.choice: over all his works: reaching all he has made
decisions.reason: His compassion rests on every creature, not only on Israel; verses 15-16 show it in the food he gives to all that lives.

source.text: יוֹד֣וּךָ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וַ֝חֲסִידֶ֗יךָ יְבָרֲכֽוּכָה׃

records.literal_gloss: They will thank you, YHWH, all your works, and your faithful [ones] will bless you.

en.L: All {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful [ones] will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful people will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Your faithful people will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: all your works: all that God has made
decisions.reason: Creation itself gives thanks by what it is, as in 19:2 and 148; God's faithful people give thanks in words.

decisions.choice: the faithful: people of loyal love
decisions.reason: The word (chasidim) is related to chesed, loyal love: people who hold fast to the LORD in love and loyalty (4:4).

source.text: כְּב֣וֹד מַלְכוּתְךָ֣ יֹאמֵ֑רוּ וּגְבוּרָתְךָ֥ יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] glory of your kingdom they will speak, and your might they will tell,

en.L: The glory of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom they will tell, and [of] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might they will speak,
en.B: They will speak of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glorious reign and tell of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power,
en.R: They will talk about how glorious {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom is. They will tell about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power.

decisions.choice: your kingdom: your rule as King
decisions.reason: The word (malkhut) is the royal rule of God more than a territory. Verses 11-13 speak of the kingdom four times; the psalm opened with "my God, the King".
Verse 12 gives the purpose of this telling, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
"They" are the faithful of verse 10.

source.text: לְהוֹדִ֤יעַ׀לִבְנֵ֣י הָ֭אָדָם גְּבוּרֹתָ֑יו וּ֝כְב֗וֹד הֲדַ֣ר מַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: to make known to [the] sons of humankind his mighty deeds and [the] glory of [the] splendor of his kingdom.

en.L: to make known to the sons of humankind {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty deeds and the glory of the splendor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom.
en.B: to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty acts known to all people, and the glorious splendor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} reign.
en.R: They want all people to know about the powerful things God has done and how glorious and wonderful {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom is.

decisions.reason: The psalm turns from speaking to God ("your kingdom") to speaking about him ("his kingdom"), because these words are what is told to other people.

decisions.choice: the sons of humankind: human beings
decisions.reason: "Sons of adam" is an ordinary way of saying people, men and women (11:4).
Readable starts a new sentence, so it names who wants this, the faithful of verse 10, and names God, whom the Hebrew calls "his".

source.text: מַֽלְכוּתְךָ֗ מַלְכ֥וּת כָּל־עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וּ֝מֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֗ בְּכָל־דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Your kingdom [is] a kingdom of all ages, and your dominion [is] in every generation and generation.

en.L: Your kingdom [is] a kingdom of all ages, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dominion [is] in every generation and generation.
en.B: Your kingdom is a kingdom for all the ages, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rule lasts through every generation.
en.R: Your kingdom will never end. You will rule over people in every age that will ever come.

decisions.choice: the missing nun line: the Hebrew text has none
alternatives: God is faithful in his words and kind in all his works (the ancient Greek translation and a Dead Sea scroll)
decisions.reason: After this verse, the line beginning with the letter nun is missing from the Hebrew text, and the Hebrew alphabet goes on with samekh in verse 14. The ancient Greek translation and the Psalms scroll from cave 11 at Qumran have a line here beginning with nun: "Faithful is God in his words, and kind (or holy) in all his works". Its second half is the same as verse 17. It may be an original line that was lost, or one written later to fill the gap. The renderings follow the Hebrew text.
The plural ('olamim) means all the ages of time, without end.
The doubled word (dor vador) means one generation after another without end.

source.text: סוֹמֵ֣ךְ יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־הַנֹּפְלִ֑ים וְ֝זוֹקֵ֗ף לְכָל־הַכְּפוּפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Supporting [is] YHWH for all those who fall, and raising up all those who are bowed down.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] supporting all those who fall, and raising up all those [who are] bowed down.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} holds up everyone who stumbles and raises all who are bent low.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} helps everyone who falls. He lifts up everyone who is weighed down with trouble.

decisions.reason: The verb (samakh) is to lean a hand on something and so to hold it up (37:17, 24).

decisions.choice: bowed down: bent over under a load
decisions.reason: The word (kefufim) is people bent down by grief or hardship; the same words "raises up the bowed down" are in 146:8.
Readable says what bends them low (m2).

source.text: עֵֽינֵי־כֹ֭ל אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּ֑רוּ וְאַתָּ֤ה נֽוֹתֵן־לָהֶ֖ם אֶת־אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] eyes of all to you look in hope, and you [are] giving to them their food in its time.

en.L: The eyes of all look to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in hope, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them their food in its time.
en.B: All eyes are turned to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in hope, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} provide their food when it is needed.
en.R: Every living thing looks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and waits. You give them their food at just the right time.

decisions.reason: Almost the same words describe every creature waiting for God to feed it in 104:27-28.
The verb (sibber) is to wait with hope for what is to come (104:27).
"All" here includes the animals, as "every living thing" in verse 16 shows.
Readable says who "all" are (m3).

source.text: פּוֹתֵ֥חַ אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַשְׂבִּ֖יעַ לְכָל־חַ֣י רָצֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Opening your hand and satisfying to every living [thing] [its] desire.

en.L: [You are] opening {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand and satisfying every living [thing with its] desire.
en.B: You open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand and give every living creature what it longs for.
en.R: You open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand wide and give every living creature all it wants.

decisions.choice: desire: what it wants, its fill
decisions.reason: The word (ratson) usually means favor or goodwill, but here it is what each creature longs for. Some read it as "with favor": God feeds them out of goodwill.
An open hand gives generously (Deuteronomy 15:8, 11).

source.text: צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֑יו וְ֝חָסִ֗יד בְּכָל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Righteous [is] YHWH in all his ways, and faithful in all his works.

en.L: Righteous [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and faithful in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works.
en.B: In all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is righteous; in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is faithful.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does what is right in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does. He is loving and loyal in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} acts.

decisions.reason: The word (chasid) is the one used for God's faithful people in verse 10, from chesed, loyal love. Used of God (as in Jeremiah 3:12) it means that he acts with loyal love.

decisions.choice: ways: the paths he takes, what he does
decisions.reason: God's "ways" are his actions and the way he deals with people (18:31).
Readable says what "righteous" means.

source.text: קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Near [is] YHWH to all who call him, to all who call him in truth.

en.L: Near [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to all who call [on] {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to all who call [on] {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in truth.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is close to everyone who calls to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to all who call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} sincerely.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is close to everyone who prays to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is near to all who pray to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and mean it.

decisions.reason: The word ('emet) is truth and also faithfulness. To call on God "in truth" is to call with a sincere heart, not with words alone (Isaiah 29:13).

decisions.choice: call him: call to him for help
decisions.reason: To call on God is to pray to him, especially in need (verse 19).
Readable uses the everyday word for calling on God.

source.text: רְצוֹן־יְרֵאָ֥יו יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְֽאֶת־שַׁוְעָתָ֥ם יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְיוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] desire of those who fear him he does, and their cry he hears and he saves them.

en.L: The desire of those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, and their cry {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves them.
en.B: He grants what those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} desire; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears their cry for help and rescues them.
en.R: He gives people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} what they want. When they cry for help, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears and saves them.

decisions.choice: those who fear him: people who honor God
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to hold him in awe, trust him and obey him (34:10).
The word (shav'ah) is a call for help in trouble (18:7).
Readable says what this kind of fear is (m1).

source.text: שׁוֹמֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה אֶת־כָּל־אֹהֲבָ֑יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הָרְשָׁעִ֣ים יַשְׁמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: Keeping [is] YHWH all who love him, and all the wicked he will destroy.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] keeping all who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but all the wicked {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} guards everyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wipe out all the wicked.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} protects everyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy all wicked people.

decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) is a guard's watching over what is in his care (121:3-8).
The "and" joins two opposite outcomes, as in 1:6, so it is "but" here.

source.text: תְּהִלַּ֥ת יְהוָ֗ה יְֽדַבֶּ֫ר־פִּ֥י וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ כָּל־בָּ֭שָׂר שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשׁ֗וֹ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] praise of YHWH my mouth will speak, and let all flesh bless [the] name of his holiness forever and ever.

en.L: The praise of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my mouth will speak, and let all flesh bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name forever and ever.
en.B: With my own mouth I will speak praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; may all creatures bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name for all time to come.
en.R: I will speak words of praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let every living thing praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name forever and ever!

decisions.reason: "All flesh" means everything that lives (Genesis 6:12-13; 136:25), or here perhaps all people. The psalm ends where verse 1 began, with blessing God's name, but now the call is for all to join in.

decisions.choice: the name of his holiness: his holy name
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying "his holy name" (103:1).
Balanced and Readable say what "all flesh" means (m1).
